Curator Backtest (CBT)

2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22

The watchlist-curator agent was called biweekly over the 2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22 window. At each rebalance it read a date-clean news pool for the preceding biweekly window (built upstream from GDELT GKG + Wayback, look-ahead-reduced; browse them in the pool browser) and proposed adds and removes against the active watchlist; the optimizer then ran mean-variance on the revised watchlist. Each rebalance is marked by an orange square on the curator curve in chart 2 — hover over one to see that rebalance's adds, removes, and the curator's rationale. The buy-and-hold curve below is the value of the initial portfolio (which never gets rebalanced or optimized) over time. The buy-and-hold portfolio has equal amounts of [AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN] and is held without any rebalancing across the window. Throughout the charts below: general_markets = defensive equity ETFs (broad-market / dividend / utilities / staples); cashlike = bonds + cash-equivalents + precious metals (e.g., AGG, BIL, IAU).

2023-09-30 — no changes · 18 queries

Rationale: The news pool for late September 2023 contains substantial wave-relevant activity, but on close inspection most candidates fail investability or quality filters. Key findings: (1) Nuclear: uranium miners (CCJ, URA constituents) are running on spot price momentum ($60+/lb), but the profile explicitly excludes commodity plays without differentiated technology exposure; SMR developers (OKLO, BWXT) are already held. The US microreactor MARVEL test and Polish plant design contract are government/academic milestones without new public-market vehicles. (2) Rockets/spacecraft: RKLB is held; SpaceX and ispace are private; Boeing (BA) is a legacy prime without pure-play space exposure. The Rocket Lab failure (Sept 19) is a negative signal, not an add catalyst. (3) Robotics: Tesla (TSLA) Optimus update is already held via the broad tech allocation; Sarcos (STRC) is a micro-cap with no fresh contract news; Mujin and Intrinsic (Alphabet) are private. (4) Quantum: IonQ (IONQ) is the only US-listed pure-play with real news (UMD QLab opening, USSOCOM CRADA), but it is not yet held and merits consideration. However, the profile's quantum wave is explicitly 'early buildup' with commercial impact years away; IONQ at ~$15 (post-2021 SPAC) has already re-rated substantially and lacks a near-term revenue inflection in this window. Given 8 free slots, the discipline is to wait for a clearer entry or a more decisive catalyst rather than fill a slot with a name that has already run. (5) Geo-defense/geo-drones: Elbit (ESLT), AeroVironment (AVAV) are held; Teledyne (TDY) is held; remaining names are foreign, private, or micro-caps without liquidity. (6) Demographics: eldercare REITs and Alzheimer's plays (BIIB, ESALY) surfaced but are either held (LLY, GEHC) or foreign/OTC. (7) Tankers: multiple headlines on US government boosting tanker fleet access, but the profile's geo_tankers wave is explicitly tactical with a 2026 Iran-deal unwind narrative that does not yet apply in September 2023; pure-play tankers (FRO, EURN, STNG) are commodity cyclicals without the 'early buildup' profile sought. Net assessment: no ticker meets the threshold of 'fresh catalyst + early buildup + US-listed + liquid + not already held.' The watchlist maintains its current shape; the optimizer can weight existing names while awaiting clearer new-wave entry points.
